speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me when these symptoms started and if they are constant or come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the mechanism of injury involving a forceful pull suggests a potential tendon or ligament injury. Does the pain make it difficult to extend or flex that finger, and is there any visible deformity?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (extensor tendon rupture).

The clinical picture of an inability to flex the DIP joint, pain at that specific joint, and the finger resting in extension following a forced pull is classic for this injury. I am requesting the X-ray results to rule out an associated avulsion fracture. REQUEST TEST: Hand_X_Ray_Ring

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
